Glycolysis, mitochondrial metabolism, lipid and amino-acid pathways in supporting HSC and AML cell function

HSCs (top) and AML cells (bottom) rely on distinct yet overlapping metabolic pathways to sustain their function. HIF-1α enhances glycolysis by promoting pyruvate conversion to lactate through LDHA and activates PDK to downregulate oxidative metabolism by inhibiting PDH-mediated entry of pyruvate into the TCA cycle. FAO fuels the TCA cycle, where long-chain fatty acids are activated to fatty acyl-CoA in the cytosol and transported into mitochondria by the carnitine shuttle (CPT1/2), generating acetyl-CoA in both HSCs and leukaemic cells. Choline fuels lipid production in HSCs by supporting synthesis of the membrane lipids phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin. In AML cells, amino-acid metabolism further supports mitochondrial function. Glutamine is converted to glutamate by glutaminase (GLS) and subsequently to α-ketoglutarate (αKG) to replenish the TCA cycle, while cysteine contributes to reduced glutathione (GSH) synthesis to support succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activity. BCAAs are catabolized by BCAT1 to generate branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs), which enter the TCA cycle as acetyl-CoA or succinyl-CoA (SucCoA). BCAT1 upregulation depletes αKG and suppresses DNA methylation in AML. Aspartate/glutamate carriers (AGC1/2) mediate amino-acid exchange between the cytosol and mitochondria in HSCs. Cytosolic oxaloacetate (OAA) is converted to malate, imported by the 2-oxoglutarate carrier (OGC), reconverted to OAA, and then transformed into aspartate by GOT2. NADH and FADH2 generated by the TCA cycle and FAO fuel OXPHOS, in which ETC complexes I–IV generate the mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψmt) used by complex V for ATP synthesis. In AML, mitochondrial proteases CLPP and neurolysin (NLN) preserve mitochondrial integrity by degrading damaged proteins. Notably, ETC complex IV activity is reduced in AML cells compared with HSCs. CoQ, coenzyme Q; Cyt c, cytochrome c; glucose-6-P, glucose-6-phosphate; PEP, phosphoenolpyruvate
